--- title: "[SmoothHRResult]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Smooth non-linear hazard ratio curve for a continuous covariate. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_cox.py#L211-L341){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python SmoothHRResult( term, reference, grid, log_hr, hr, log_hr_lower, log_hr_upper, hr_lower, hr_upper, df, knots, adjustment ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Contains the estimated log-hazard ratio (and hazard ratio) as a function of a continuous covariate, computed by refitting the Cox model with a B-spline basis expansion. The curve shows how the covariate's effect on the hazard varies across its range, relative to a reference value. ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [term]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the covariate whose smooth effect is estimated. [reference]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Reference value of the covariate. The log-HR is zero at this point. [grid]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of covariate values at which the curve is evaluated. [log_hr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Log hazard ratio at each grid point (relative to ``reference``). [hr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Hazard ratio at each grid point (``exp(log_hr)``). [log_hr_lower]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Lower confidence bound on the log-HR. [log_hr_upper]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Upper confidence bound on the log-HR. [hr_lower]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Lower confidence bound on the HR (``exp(log_hr_lower)``). [hr_upper]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Upper confidence bound on the HR (``exp(log_hr_upper)``). [df]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Degrees of freedom of the spline (number of basis functions). [knots]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Interior knot positions used for the B-spline basis. [adjustment]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary of covariate names and the values they were held at. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Estimate a smooth hazard ratio curve for age from a Cox model fit on the `lung` dataset. The curve shows how the hazard changes across the range of age, relative to the median: ::: {#1463897f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(time="time", event="status", data=lung, event_value=2) cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(y, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=lung) shr = cox.smooth_hr(term="age") shr ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` SmoothHRResult(term='age', reference=62.44736842105263, df=4, grid=200 points) ``` ::: ::: Convert the curve to a DataFrame on the hazard-ratio scale: ::: {#74cbba2c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} shr.to_frame(scale="hr", format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

### [to_frame()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the smooth curve as a DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_cox.py#L305-L341){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python to_frame(*, scale="log_hr", format=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["log_hr"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"log_hr"` (the default) returns log hazard ratios and confidence bounds. `"hr"` returns hazard ratios (exponentiated). [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [`pandas.DataFrame`, `polars.DataFrame`, or `pyarrow.Table`]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Export the smooth hazard ratio curve on the log-HR scale (the default): ::: {#3fbbe42c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(time="time", event="status", data=lung, event_value=2) cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(y, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=lung) shr = cox.smooth_hr(term="age") shr.to_frame(format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
